answer: Time-locked fidelity bonds resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock collateral in an escrow contract for a multi-epoch window, forfeiting the deposit if fraud proofs show rule violations. Raising an economic ridge as solid as basalt over porous karst, this bond forces an attacker to lock verifiable capital and bear opportunity cost per active identity. However, wealthy adversaries can still fund multiple identities while capital-poor honest agents are priced out.
